sheets.text:
ASHOKAN INSCRIPTIONS

Classification

1\. Rock inscriptions 2. Pillar inscriptions 3. Cave inscriptions

Major Rock Edict Sites

o Shahbazgarhi o Mansehra o Kalsi o Girnar o Dhauli o Jaugada o Yerragudi o Sopara

Language and Script

• Most inscriptions → Prakrit + Brahmi

• Shahbazgarhi → Kharosthi

• Mansehra → Kharosthi

• Taxila → Aramaic

• Kandahar/Shar-i-Kuna → Greek + Aramaic

• Laghman → Aramaic

Site Script Most Ashokan inscriptions Brahmi Shahbazgarhi Kharosthi Mansehra Kharosthi Taxila Aramaic Kandahar Greek + Aramaic Laghman Aramaic

BRAHMI & KHAROSTHI

Brahmi

• Most Ashokan inscriptions → Brahmi

• Deciphered by → James Prinsep

• James Prinsep → First scholar to read Ashoka's edicts.

James Prinsep → Brahmi → Ashokan inscrip ons

Kharosthi

• Direction → Right to left

• Region → North-western India

• Major Ashokan examples: o Shahbazgarhi o Mansehra

Kharosthi → NW India → Right to Left

ASHOKA'S NAME

• Ashoka generally referred to as: o Priyadarshi/Piyadasi o Devanampiya Piyadasi

• Meaning → Beloved of the Gods

Personal name "Ashoka" occurs in:

• Maski

• Gujarra

• Nettur

• Udagolam

⭐ Most important: Maski → Personal name Ashoka

IMPORTANT ASHOKAN INSCRIPTIONS

Rummindei / Lumbini Pillar

• Ruler → Ashoka

• Place → Lumbini

• Marks → Birthplace of Buddha

• Ashoka visited → After 20th year of coronation

• Bali tax exempted

• Land revenue → 1/6 → 1/8

Rummindei → Lumbini → Buddha's birthplace

Bhabru / Bairat Inscription

• Ashoka's association with → Buddhism

• Ashoka's title → Piyadasi Raja

• Associated with → King of Magadha

Bhabru → Ashoka → Buddhism

Kanganahalli Inscription

• Place → Karnataka, Bhima River

• Stone portrait → Ashoka + queen

• Inscription → “Ranyo Ashoka”

• Meaning → King Ashoka

⭐ Ranyo Ashoka → Kanganahalli

Kalsi Rock Edicts

• Place → Dehradun, Uttarakhand

• Associated with → Ashokan Rock Edicts

Kalsi → Rock Edicts

ASHOKA'S MAJOR ROCK EDICTS

Rock Edict I

• Concern → Animal slaughter/sacrifice

• Royal kitchen → Gradual reduc on and eventual stopping of animal killing.

RE I → Animal slaughter

Rock Edict II

Mentions:

• Chola

• Pandya

• Satiyaputta

• Keralaputta

• Tamraparni/Sri Lanka

Also → Medical treatment for humans + animals

RE II → South India + Medical care

Rock Edict XII

• Religious tolerance

• Respect for different religious sects.

RE XII → Religious harmony

Rock Edict XIII

• Kalinga War

• War → 8th year after coronation

• Date → 261 BC

• Ashoka's → Remorse

• Shift → Military conquest → Dhamma conquest

• Mentions Greek/Yavana rulers

RE XIII → Kalinga + Remorse + Greeks + Dhamma

BOGHAZ-KOI INSCRIPTION

• Place → Asia Minor (present-day Turkey)

• Date → 14th century BC

• Mentions Vedic gods:

o Indra o Varuna o Mitra o Nasatya

Boghaz-Koi → Vedic Gods → Indra–Varuna–Mitra–Nasatya

SOHGAURA & MAHASTHAN

Sohgaura Copper Plate

• Place → Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh

• Period → Mauryan

• Described as → Earliest known copper plate

• Concern → Food-grain preservation

• Context → Famine/crisis

Sohgaura → Copper plate → Grain → Famine

Mahasthan Inscription

• Place → Bogura, Bangladesh

• Concern → Famine relief

Mahasthan → Famine relief

JUNAGADH INSCRIPTION — RUDRADAMAN

• Ruler → Rudradaman I

• Place → Girnar/Junagadh, Gujarat

• Date → c. 150 AD

• Language → Sanskrit

• Script → Brahmi

• Important for → Sudarshan Lake

Sudarshan Lake

• Originally constructed by → Pushyagupta, governor of Chandragupta Maurya

• Canals → Tushasp, governor of Ashoka

• Repaired by → Rudradaman

Special Features

• Earliest perfect Sanskrit inscription

• Early specimen of Kavya style

• Repair of Sudarshan Lake → without forced labour

⭐ Junagadh → Rudradaman → Sanskrit → Brahmi → Sudarshan Lake

HATHIGUMPHA INSCRIPTION

• Ruler → Kharavela

• Dynasty → Chedi/Mahameghavahana

• Region → Kalinga

• Place → Udayagiri caves, Odisha

• Major source for → Kharavela's history

• Records → 13 years of reign

• Religion → Jainism

• Mentions → Nanda ruler/Mahapadmananda

• Also → Canal ac vity, dona ons to Jain monks, southern victories.

Hathigumpha → Kharavela → Kalinga → Jainism

Evidence for Nanda ruler → Hathigumpha

AYODHYA INSCRIPTION

• Associated with → Pushyamitra Shunga

• Pushyamitra performed → 2 Ashvamedha Yajnas

Ayodhya → Pushyamitra → 2 Ashvamedhas

SATAVAHANA INSCRIPTIONS

Nanaghat

• Dynasty → Satavahana

• Important for → Satakarni-I's governance

Nanaghat → Satavahana administra on

• Title → Ekabrahmana

• Interpretation → Unrivalled Brahmana

Nashik → Gautamiputra → Ekabrahmana

KANISHKA INSCRIPTIONS

Sarnath Buddhist Image Inscription

• Ruler → Kanishka

• Place → Sarnath

• Date → 81 AD

• Established → 3 years after corona on.

Sarnath → Kanishka → 81 AD

• Ruler → Kanishka

• Place → Afghanistan

• Script → Greek

Cities:

Shravasti not mentioned

PRAYAG PRASHASTI / ALLAHABAD PILLAR

• Ruler → Samudragupta

• Author → Harisena

• Language → Sanskrit

• Script → Brahmi

• Nature → Panegyric/eulogy

• Records → Poli cal & military achievements, southern expedi ons, Dakshinapatha rulers.

• Koshala ruler mentioned → Mahendra

Allahabad Pillar — 4 Inscriptions

1\. Ashokan inscription 2. Queen's Edict → Karuvaki 3. Samudragupta → Harisena 4. Jahangir → Persian

• Originally associated with → Ashoka

• Originally located at → Kaushambi

• Shifted to Allahabad/Prayagraj by → Akbar

Allahabad Pillar → Ashoka + Karuvaki + Samudragupta + Jahangir

GUPTA INSCRIPTIONS

Mehrauli Iron Pillar

• King → Chandra

• Identified as → Chandragupta II

• Devoted to → Vishnu

• Established → Vishnu Dhvaja

• Associated with → Vishnupada

Mehrauli → Chandra → Chandragupta II → Vishnu

Bhitari Pillar

• Ruler → Skandagupta

• Place → Ghazipur, U.P.

• Concern → Huna invasion/war

Bhitari → Skandagupta → Hunas

Eran Inscription

• First inscriptional evidence of → Sati

• Date → 510 AD

• Woman → Wife of military commander Gopraj

Eran → Sa → 510 AD → Gopraj

MANDSAUR / DASHPUR INSCRIPTION

• Ruler → Kumaragupta I

• Place → Mandsaur/Dashpur, Malwa

• Associated with → Silk-weavers guild

• Silk weavers → Tantuwayas

• Guild from → Lata region/Gujarat

• Built → Sun Temple

• Governor → Bandhuvarman

• Composer → Vatsabhatti

Mandsaur → Kumaragupta → Silk guild → Sun Temple → Vatsabha

GWALIOR INSCRIPTION

Mihirakula

• Gwalior inscription → Territory of Mihirakula

Nagabhata I

• Associated with → Gurjara-Pratiharas

• Destroyed army of → Mlechcha ruler

• Interpreted in source as probably Arab ruler of Sindh.

Gwalior → Mihirakula / Nagabhata I

AIHOLE INSCRIPTION

• Ruler → Pulakeshin II

• Place → Aihole, Karnataka

• Composer → Ravikirti

• Language → Sanskrit

• Script → Southern Brahmi

Important

• Pulakeshin II vs → Harshavardhana

• Harsha's southward expansion stopped at → Narmada

• Mentions → Kalidasa

• Also mentions → Bharavi

• Gurjaras → Men oned.

Aihole → Pulakeshin II → Ravikir → Harsha → Kalidasa

BADAMI & LOHNARA

Badami Rock Inscription

• Ruler → Pulakeshin I

• Date → Saka 465

Lohnara Inscription

• Ruler → Pulakeshin II

• Date → 630 AD

• Harsha NOT mentioned

Lohnara → Harsha absent Aihole → Harsha men oned

SONDANI INSCRIPTION

• Ruler → Yashodharman

• Composer → Vasula Kavi

Sondani → Yashodharman → Vasula Kavi

MAUKHARI COPPER-SEAL

• Ruler → Sarvavarman

• Found at → Asirgarh Fort, M.P.

• Gives → Maukhari genealogy

• Begins with → Harivarman

Sarvavarman → Asirgarh → Maukhari genealogy

CHAUSATH YOGINI TEMPLE INSCRIPTION

• Place → Morena, M.P.

• Date → 1323 CE

• Dynasty → Kachchhapaghata

• Ruler → Devapala

• Records → Devapala built the temple.

CHOLA INSCRIPTIONS

Uttaramerur

• Dynasty → Chola

• Famous for → Village administration

• Includes:

o Sabha o Village assemblies o Local committees o Committee selection/working

⭐ Uttaramerur → Chola → Local self-government

Thanjavur

• Ruler → Rajaraja I

• Records → Military achievements

• Defeat of → Chera naval force at Kandallur

• Also reflects → Chola overseas expansion

Thanjavur → Rajaraja I → Chera naval defeat

Chola Temple Inscriptions

• Rajaraja I + Rajendra I → Temple-wall inscriptions.

• Recorded → Victories and achievements.

• Major reason Chola history is well documented → Extensive temple inscriptions.

PALA INSCRIPTIONS

Khalimpur Inscription

• Ruler → Dharmapala

• Mentions selection/election of → Gopala

• Reason → End Matsya Nyaya

• Matsya Nyaya → Law of the Jungle

Khalimpur → Dharmapala → Gopala → Matsya Nyaya

Dharmapala

• Title → Param Saugat

• Indicates → Buddhist affiliation

MOTUPALLI EPIGRAPH

• Concern → Trade + tariff rates

• Commodities include:

o Sandal o Camphor o Rose water

o Ivory o Pearls o Corals o Copper o Zinc o Lead o Silk o Pepper o Areca nuts

⭐ Evidence → Imports and exports through Motupalli port

Motupalli → Port trade → Commodity tariff

SANJAN & RADHANPUR COPPER PLATES

• Ruler → Govinda III

• Dynasty → Rashtrakuta

• Records victory over → Nagabhata II

• Dynasty defeated → Gurjara-Pratihara

Sanjan + Radhanpur → Govinda III → Nagabhata II defeated

GARDHMUKTESHWAR INSCRIPTION

• Ruler → Balban

• Place → Garhmukteshwar Mosque

• Balban called himself → “Helper of a Caliph”

⭐ Garhmukteshwar → Balban → Helper of a Caliph

MEDIEVAL COINS — INSCRIPTIONS

Mahmud Ghazni

• Silver coins:

o One side → Arabic o Other side → Sanskrit

• Sanskrit script → Devanagari

Muhammad Ghori

• One side → Goddess Lakshmi

• Other side → Kalma in Arabic

Iltutmish

• After Caliph's recognition → Caliph's name on coins

Alauddin Khalji

• Title → Sikandar-i-Sani

• Inscribed on → Coins

Muhammad bin Tughluq

• Coin legend → “Al Sultan Zilli Allah”

• Meaning → Sultan as Shadow of God

sheets.heading: BUDDHA & CONTEMPORARIES
sheets.text:
BUDDHA & CONTEMPORARIES

Gautama Buddha was contemporary with:

• Bimbisara → King of Magadha

• Prasenjit → King of Kosala

• Mahavira → Jain Tirthankara

• Makkhali Gosala → Leader of the Ajivika sect

ALEXANDER'S CONTEMPORARY

• Dhanananda, the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, was a contemporary of Alexander.

• Greek writers referred to him as: Agrammese

• His commander was: Bhaddasala

PATANJALI

• Patanjali ↔ Pushyamitra Shunga

• Patanjali, the author of Mahabhashya, was a contemporary of Pushyamitra Shunga.

KANISHKA'S CONTEMPORARIES

Kanishka ↔ Ashvaghosha

Ashvaghosha was associated with the court of Kanishka.

Important works:

• Buddhacharita

• Saundarananda

Kanishka ↔ Vasumitra

• Vasumitra was associated with Kanishka's court and headed the Fourth Buddhist Council.

Other scholars associated with Kanishka's court

• Nagarjuna

• Charaka

• Parsva

• Mathara

Kanishka → Ashvaghosha + Vasumitra + Nagarjuna + Charaka

HARSHAVARDHANA'S CONTEMPORARIES

Harsha ↔ Banabhatta

• Banabhatta was the court poet of Harsha.

• He wrote: Harshacharita

Harsha → Banabha a → Harshacharita

Harsha ↔ Xuanzang

• Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana.
